newsitem.title: USA: Integon to reduce entry into new markets.
newsitem.headline: Integon to reduce entry into new markets.

text.p: Integon Corp, which reported disappointing third quarter earnings, said it will be reducing the number of new states it plans to enter in 1997 so it can concentrate on further profitable penetration of existing markets.

Integon reported third quarter earnings of $0.22 a share compared to Wall Street's consensus estimate of $0.38 a share. Excluding the impact of Hurricanes Bertha and Fran, operating earnings would have been $0.31 a share.
Integon reported earnings of $0.51 a share a year ago.
"We have several significant markets that have contributed to the decline in earnings," Integon chief executive James Lambie said in a statement.
"In these markets, we have recently taken rate increases and are continuing to aggressively manage agencies to terminate relationships that are unprofitable," he added.

The entry into fewer new states along with the rate increases and agency management "should put earnings back on track and also bring the premium growth rate closer to our targeted 20 percent level," Lambie said.
Net premiums written in the third quarter grew 31 percent compared to the same quarter in 1995.
"Although we have taken significant rate action during 1996, the growth has not slowed," Lambie said.
Integon said the expense ratio was up slightly in the third quarter to 21.9 percent from 21.6 percent a year ago.
We don't expect expense ratio improvement in the near term, as we increase our investment in technology to enable us to rapidly implement our systems strategies," Lambie said.

"This increased investment in technology will, we believe, lead to longer-term savings that will ultimately reduce the expense ratio, make it easier for agents to do business with us and enhance customer service," he said.
Lambie said he was still confident the company can achieve its long-term goals of net premiums written growth of 20 percent and a combined ratio below 96 percent.
The GAAP combined ratio, excluding the impact of Hurricanes Fran and Bertha, would have been 96.9 percent.
"This quarter is the first out of the last seven consecutive quarters that the combined ratio has exceeded 96.0 percent after adjustment for catastrophes," Lambie said.
